title: DuckDNS
descript: DuckDNS is a free dynamic DNS service. It keeps a name like mynas.duckdns.org pointed at the public IP of your NAS, so you can reach it when your ISP changes that address. This package runs the official LinuxServer.io DuckDNS client, which checks the address every few minutes and calls the DuckDNS API when it changes. A built-in page lets you enter the subdomain and token and shows the last update result. The container runs as a non-root user and keeps its settings and log in the application data folder.
important: Requires DockerEngine. Create a domain/token at duckdns.org, enter the subdomain (without .duckdns.org) and token, and save. Keep the token secret; it is stored in DockerAppData/duckdnsdocker/config/duckdns.conf (app user only). The app sends the subdomain, token and IP to duckdns.org; see the privacy policy. It only updates DNS; remote access still needs port forwarding or a tunnel. Plain HTTP on the LAN with no login; keep it off the internet. Back up the folder before uninstalling.
release_note: 2026.11.2-2: added a privacy policy covering the DuckDNS update API and the optional Cloudflare address lookup, and linked it from the help field. Rectified per review comments C3-C8.

zh-hk.descript: DuckDNS 是一個免費的動態域名服務。它把 mynas.duckdns.org 這樣的域名始終指向 NAS 的公網 IP，即使網路供應商更換位址，仍可從外網存取。本應用執行 LinuxServer.io 官方 DuckDNS 用戶端，每隔幾分鐘偵測一次位址，位址變更時呼叫 DuckDNS 更新介面。內建頁面可以填寫子域名與 Token，並顯示最近一次更新的結果。容器以非 root 使用者執行，設定與日誌都儲存在應用程式資料目錄。
zh-hk.important: 需要 DockerEngine。請在 duckdns.org 建立域名並取得 Token，填寫子域名（不含 .duckdns.org）與 Token 後儲存。Token 儲存在 DockerAppData/duckdnsdocker/config/duckdns.conf，僅應用程式使用者可讀，請視同密鑰保管。應用會把子域名、Token 和 IP 傳送到 duckdns.org，詳見隱私政策。它只更新 DNS；外網存取仍需連接埠轉送或內網穿透。頁面是區域網路明文 HTTP 且沒有登入，請勿暴露到公網。解除安裝前請備份該目錄。

data_notes: Everything persistent lives in `/config`: `duckdns.conf` holds the subdomain(s), token, IP-detection mode and check interval; `duckdns.log` keeps the last lines of updater output; `status` is the result of the last run. Copying the config folder is a complete backup.
design_notes: **Runs as a non-root container.** The upstream image starts s6-overlay as root; this entrypoint bypasses s6 and invokes the image's own `/app/duck.sh` directly as uid 1000, so no root and no privilege drop are involved.

**A real page for a client that has none.** The upstream image ships no web server, and a TOS Docker app must open a page. The entrypoint serves a self-contained status and setup page with the busybox `nc` that is already in the image - no extra container, no extra image, nothing installed at runtime.

**Upstream client, not a reimplementation.** Every update is still performed by the image's own `/app/duck.sh`, with the subdomain, token and IP mode exported from `/config/duckdns.conf`; the wrapper only schedules it and reports the result.
**Health check** probes `/healthz`; it stays healthy while DuckDNS is unconfigured or the last update failed, so an upstream outage cannot get the app disabled by the platform.
**No secret in the package.** The subdomain and token live only in the mounted data folder (`/config/duckdns.conf`, mode 600), never in the compose file.

**Privacy.** The app sends only the subdomain, token and detected IP to duckdns.org (and a DNS query to Cloudflare in the optional ipv4/ipv6 modes). It sends no telemetry; `PRIVACY.md` documents this and is linked from the package Help field.
limitations: The app only updates the DuckDNS record. It does not open firewall ports, so remote access still needs port forwarding or a tunnel.
Outbound HTTPS to www.duckdns.org is required; the optional Cloudflare IP-detection modes also need access to 1.1.1.1 / 2606:4700:4700::1111 over DNS.
The page is plain HTTP on the LAN and has no login. Do not publish the port to the internet.
The DuckDNS token is stored in plain text in the application data folder, readable only by the application user (mode 600). Treat the folder as a secret and back it up accordingly.
One DuckDNS token per instance. Several subdomains under that token can be updated together.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center: updating means uninstalling and reinstalling, which keeps the data folder.
